newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares battered by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares battered by profit-taking.

text.p: Danish share prices, after rising almost four percent since the start of October, were deflated by profit-taking for the second day on Thursday and dealers saw more losses Friday, with a rebound next week.
"We saw continued profit-taking today, exacerbated by a weak bond market. The undertone is still positive though, so the market will rise again sure enough," a trader said.

The KFX top-20 index lost 0.14 point to 128.18 in overall bourse turnover of 778 million crowns. The KFX December future was untraded at 129.40. News of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed's dismissal emerged only after the market closed.
Sophus Berendsen continued to buck the down-trend on the strength of warm bank recommendations and climbed five crowns to 731.84.
Den Danske Bank gained two crowns to 437, despite the adverse bond market, but Unidanmark fell four crowns to 283.

A newly-published Unidanmark analysis advised investors to buy Carlsberg up to 400 crowns, despite the endorsement the megabrewer's share fell four crowns to 377 crowns. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969651
